design.rule: mean AUC over the last 3 21-session blocks before the anchor (each block: rolling 504-session training window ending 22 sessions before its first session, exit-date purge against that session); best mean wins (ties: grid order, incumbent first) but the incumbent is kept unless the best beats it by >= 0.002; a year without 3 blocks whose training windows hold >= 120 sessions keeps the incumbent
design.outer_test_data_used: inner rows are dated <= the year's anchor (fold Y-01 train_end); 9 inner scoring rows (tickers with missing sessions) have labels that exit on or after the outer test start, and audit_inner_exit shows that no year's choice depends on them

audit_inner_exit.added: after the selection ran (post-hoc audit; no choice was revised)
audit_inner_exit.rule: an inner block that ends at the anchor can hold rows whose label exit date (the ticker's row t+21) is on or after the first test session of the outer fold Y-01 (tickers with missing sessions); the outer fold purges such rows from its training, the inner scoring (every clean labelled row of the block, as the design defines it) keeps them.  Removing k_pos of P positives and k_neg of N negatives changes a block's AUC by at most k_pos/P + k_neg/N; a setting's 3-block mean by at most B = the mean of that over the 3 blocks; a difference of two settings' means by at most 2B.  A kept incumbent cannot flip if every (setting - incumbent) + 2B < margin; a switch cannot flip if (best - incumbent) - 2B >= margin and the best leads every other setting by more than 2B
audit_inner_exit.exact_rule: where the bound cannot rule out a flip, every setting is refitted on each affected block (same seed, rows and threads; the refit must reproduce the cached AUC) and the block is re-scored without the rows; the selection rule is then re-applied

select_runtime.note: more than one run means the selection was stopped (container restart) and resumed from the cache
